newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Experts say child sex abuse spreading in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Experts say child sex abuse spreading in Latin America.

text.p: Child sex abuse and prostitution are rising in Latin America and children are most threatened in Brazil, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Venezuela and Cuba, United Nations officials said on Wednesday.
"Without a doubt, those are the countries where the problem is most prevalent," Brazil's UNICEF delegate Arabela Rota said at an international conference on crimes against children in Buenos Aires.
"Poverty and race ... are decisive. It is mainly poor, black women who suffer the worst abuse," she added.
The three-day conference organised by Interpol was attended by 200 experts from around the world.
The Inter-American Institute for Children's Rodrigo Quintana said sexual exploitation of minors has been rising for the past 10 years.

The reason for this is "a lack of social protection" and growing numbers of tourists from developed countries who come to Latin America on sex tours, according to Agnes Fournier de Saint Maur of Interpol's general secretariat.

In Brazil, the government has launched a strong campaign to control Brazil's booming sexual tourism industry. Streets, airports and hotels show banners that read: "Explotation of minors for sexual tourism: Beware, Brazil is watching you."

"Charter tours come from Germany, Italy, Switzerland and France," said Ana Quental, a campaign organiser. "We're talking about lower class tourists without much purchasing power. Apart from abusing our girls, they leave very little money in the country."

Rota noted sexual trade in children is blatant on the streets of Brazilian cities, especially in northern cities like Fortaleza and Bahia, and criticised Latin America' widespread free market economies which neglect social policies.
Fournier said around one million children are forced into prostitution around the world and "pedophilia is rising ... We must make governments and society aware of it."
She said of 48 cases of missing children traced by Interpol, 23 were in Brazil and 16 were raped before dying.
Asked about conditions in Argentina, Buenos Aires provincial police chief Adrian Pelacchi said pedophelia and child pornography here were "not a scourge."
